definitions.gloss: to consider; to examine; to study; to review
definitions.explanation: To carefully think about or investigate something before making a decision. Frequently used in business and formal contexts, and sometimes used as a polite way to postpone or decline a request.

examples.japanese: もう{少|すこ}し{検討|けんとう}させてください。
examples.english: Please let me think about it a bit more.

examples.japanese: その{提案|ていあん}を{社内|しゃない}で{検討|けんとう}してから{回答|かいとう}します。
examples.english: I'll review the proposal internally and then respond.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{制度|せいど}の{導入|どうにゅう}について、{委員会|いいんかい}で{慎重|しんちょう}に{検討|けんとう}した{結果|けっか}、{来年度|らいねんど}から{実施|じっし}することが{決|き}まった。
examples.english: After careful consideration by the committee regarding the introduction of the new system, it was decided to implement it from next fiscal year.

notes:
USAGE:
One of the most common business Japanese words. In practice, {検討|けんとう}します is often used as a polite way to avoid saying no directly. When someone says {検討|けんとう}します in response to a request, it can mean genuine consideration, but it can also be a soft refusal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {検討|けんとう}する{余地|よち}がある (there is room for consideration)
- {前向|まえむ}きに{検討|けんとう}する (to consider positively)
- {慎重|しんちょう}に{検討|けんとう}する (to consider carefully)
- {検討|けんとう}{結果|けっか} (result of the review)
- {検討|けんとう}{中|ちゅう} (under consideration)

NOTE FOR LEARNERS:
Be aware that {検討|けんとう}します does not always mean the matter will truly be considered. In business, it is often a diplomatic way to decline without saying no.
